rationale: D3, data-informed revision of D1. The self-extinction clock is unchanged. The weak class is decided by what the train flashes share (air injected into a lean ambient), not by the adiabatic temperature, which gave fuel-rich flames that burned for a minute a 0.94 chance of flashing. Stops that happened once (time-outs, operator decisions, unexplained ends) lose their own atoms and become a background rate, because a time seen in one session does not transfer to another; the scripted 66 s stop stays, at the frequency sessions used it. The burner-limit clock is steeper in flow and wider. Every number typed by the author from the train table; no fit, no search; nothing chosen from validation.
